methodological_rigor.justification: This is a retrospective multicenter cohort study of 1132 consecutive stage IA-B NSCLC patients undergoing curative-intent resection (2013–2021) with a minimum follow-up of 36 months. The design is appropriate for identifying associations with recurrence, and key eligibility/staging constraints are described (systematic lymph node dissection requirements and pN0 restriction). Main limitations are inherent to retrospective chart review (unmeasured confounding and potential selection effects by surgical approach), but the manuscript uses uni- and multivariable Cox regression for recurrence prediction and reports time-to-event outcomes.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is an individual cohort analysis of recurrence after surgery in early-stage NSCLC and aligns with Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high because it targets post-resection recurrence risk stratification in stage I disease, a setting where surveillance intensity and consideration of adjuvant strategies are active questions. The predictors highlighted (pT>1a and non-lepidic adenocarcinoma subtypes, and surgical approach) are directly interpretable for clinical risk discussions even if not yet a validated risk score.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is appropriate for this retrospective cohort, and the manuscript reports the multicenter setting, study period, inclusion criteria (curative resection plus lymph node dissection and >=36 months follow-up), baseline covariates, and outcome counts (224 recurrences; local vs distant breakdown). Analytic approach is described (overall/DFS analyses with uni- and multivariable Cox regression) and key multivariable predictors are stated with p-values. There is no explicit public data or code release described, consistent with multi-center clinical record data.

novelty_literature.justification: The study contributes a large contemporary multicenter dataset focused on early and late recurrence after surgery in stage I NSCLC, with recurrence timing described (e.g., events within 12 months). The identified predictors (tumor size/stage and adenocarcinoma histologic subtype patterns) are biologically plausible and consistent with prior prognostic themes, so the novelty is mainly incremental and driven by sample size and multi-center scope. The work does not introduce a new biomarker or intervention.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract clearly states the cohort size, follow-up duration, recurrence rate, and the main multivariable predictors. Methods define key surgical/pathologic criteria for inclusion and provide clinically interpretable definitions for complete resection and nodal evaluation. Results are summarized in a straightforward way with counts and p-values, supporting readability.

key_strengths: Large multicenter cohort (n=1132) with clinically meaningful endpoint (post-resection recurrence) and substantial follow-up.
Clear inclusion/staging criteria (curative-intent surgery with systematic nodal dissection; pN0 restriction) that reduce stage-migration ambiguity.
Use of uni- and multivariable Cox regression to identify independent recurrence predictors with clinically interpretable factors (pT category and adenocarcinoma subtype).
key_concerns: Retrospective design leaves residual confounding (e.g., determinants of open vs minimally invasive approach) that may influence recurrence associations.
Predictor set is limited to routinely captured variables; no molecular or radiomic features are incorporated, and no externally validated risk model is presented.
Data sharing and reproducibility details are not described, which may limit secondary validation by other groups.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a solid, clinically relevant retrospective cohort study with appropriate time-to-event analysis; it is plausible for a tier-3 journal with minor revisions focused on confounding sensitivity analyses and clearer reporting of missing data and follow-up completeness.
